description: Who took one task, when they claimed it, when they started, when they finished, what they found and what proves it. A SEPARATE DOCTYPE AND NOT A CHILD TABLE — see the controller for the arithmetic. This is the chain of custody: the answer to 'who did this and how do you know'.

fields.description: The work. A Link and not a parent, so a query for 'everything this worker is holding' is one indexed read rather than a walk over every task on the site.
fields.label: Task

fields.description: The Employee id. Data and not a Link for the same reason it is on Farm Task: Frappe HR is not a dependency of this app, and a Link would make the doctype fail to migrate on a site without it.
fields.label: Assigned To

fields.description: Claimed, In-Progress, Paused, Completed, Rejected or Merged. Rejected is a FIRST-CLASS STATE and the reason is mandatory: 'I could not get to it and dispatch never followed up' is the answer nobody can defend, and this is the field that makes it impossible to end there silently. PAUSED (v0.79.0) is the worker's — the job is still theirs and its clock is stopped; MERGED is what happens to the assignment on a duplicate whose work was folded into another task.
fields.label: State
fields.options:
Claimed
In-Progress
Paused
Completed
Rejected
Merged

fields.description: The task's title, copied at claim time so a list of somebody's work reads without a join — and so it still reads if the task is renamed afterwards.
fields.label: Task Name

fields.description: WHERE the work was actually done. FSMA §112.161(a)(1)(i) asks a record to carry the farm's name AND its location, and `task_name` is only the first half of that — a completion that says what was done and by whom, but not where, answers the question an inspector asks second. Free text on purpose: a phone that has a fix writes "45.5152,-122.6784", a phone in a metal-roofed shed writes "MC-Cabin-01", and a coordinate nobody could take is worth less than a place name somebody can stand in. Optional, and additive — completions filed before v0.19.1 have it blank and are not wrong, they are just older.
fields.label: Farm Location (GPS)
Farm Shift
fields.description: The shift this work was actually done on, and the anchor that puts the completion's evidence onto a compliance record spanning the whole exposure period. A task completion carries a point in time; the shift carries the timeline the point sits inside, and OR-OSHA asks about the second. Written at claim, start or completion — whichever first knows which shift the worker was on.

Set when a foreman put this person on the task, clear when they took it from the pool themselves. The distinction is worth keeping: work that has to be dispatched because it needs a named licence holder is a different kind of work from work anybody with the skill can pick up, and an operation that cannot tell them apart cannot staff either properly.
fields.label: Dispatched by a Foreman

fields.description: The clock-in for this task specifically. Not the same as a shift clock-in: a worker on the clock all morning did this particular cabin between ten and half past, and that is what an hour charged to a job has to mean.
fields.label: Started

fields.description: How long the work actually took, in minutes. SINCE v0.79.0 THIS IS THE SUM OF THE ACTIVE SEGMENTS and not the wall clock from start to finish. A worker who began irrigating at nine, was called to a broken valve at half past, and came back at eleven spent thirty minutes plus whatever they did after — not two hours. The wall clock would bill the valve repair to the irrigating, on exactly the fragmented afternoons where an hour charged to a job matters most. See `time_segments`.
fields.label: Actual Duration (Minutes)

fields.description: What the worker did, in their words.
fields.label: Completion Narrative

fields.description: What they FOUND, which is a different question from what they did — and the one a compliance record is built from. Blank findings on an inspection means it passed; it does not mean nobody wrote anything down.
fields.label: Findings

fields.description: Somebody else who was there and saw the same thing. Required only where the task's evidence contract asks for it — which is the work where one person's word is not the standard.
fields.label: Witness

fields.description: Why this could not be done: the equipment is broken, the conditions are unsafe, this needs a licence I do not hold. MANDATORY on a rejection, and the most useful sentence in the doctype — it is what turns 'nobody got to it' into a fact somebody can act on.
fields.label: Rejection Reason

fields.description: The signature capture, where the task asked for one.
fields.label: Signature

fields.description: The compliance record this completion produced — a Housing Inspection, a Detector Test, a Water Test. Read with the task's `creates_record` as its doctype. This is the link that makes the completion evidence rather than a status change.
fields.label: Produced Record

fields.description: Photographs and documents filed against this completion.
fields.label: Evidence Files

fields.description: The visit this completion belongs to: one identifier the handset mints when a worker arrives somewhere and reuses for every task they close before they leave. Five cabins done in one trip to the north block is ONE visit and five completions, and without this the only way to see the trip is to guess it from timestamps. A UUID as 8-4-4-4-12, matched either case — v0.20.1 accepted whatever arrived, because the app's format was not yet confirmed and refusing a completion over its least important field looked like the worse trade. It is not, now that the format is known: list_visits groups on this column by exact value, so an identifier nothing checked does not surface as a bad row, it surfaces as a SECOND VISIT, and the rollup is wrong rather than obviously incomplete. Blank on any completion filed before v0.20.1, and on any filed by a client that does not mint one; list_visits reports only completions that carry one.
fields.label: Visit

fields.description: What makes a re-sent completion recognisable as the SAME completion. A hash of the assignment, the worker, the evidence, what they wrote and the clock-out time as the client sent it — see erpnext_mcp/completions.py for what is in it and why each part. A client whose acknowledgement was lost to a dropped connection re-sends, and this is how the server answers 'you already filed this' as a success instead of as an error. Read-only: it is written by the completion that produced it, and a hand-edited signature would make a genuine conflict look like a retry.
fields.label: Completion Signature

fields.description: v0.204.0. This completion's form answers.
fields.label: Form Answers
Interruptions
fields.description: Field work is interrupted. This is where that is recorded rather than hidden inside a start and an end time that no longer mean what they say.

When the current pause began, where this assignment is paused. Cleared on resume — the history lives in `time_segments`, and a column that kept the last pause would be a second, disagreeing account of the same fact.
fields.label: Paused At

fields.description: Why the worker stopped. 'Called to the valve at Home-7' is what makes a fragmented afternoon legible six weeks later, and it is what a foreman reading a two-hour gap actually wants.
fields.label: Pause Reason

fields.description: How many times this assignment has been paused. A count rather than a derived figure so a report can sort on it: a job paused six times is a job somebody should look at, whatever its total minutes say.
fields.label: Pause Count

fields.description: Set when the SERVER paused this rather than the worker — they started another task and this one was stood down for them. Worth telling apart in front of a payroll question about a gap: nobody chose to stop.
fields.label: Auto-Paused

fields.description: Every stretch this worker was actually on this task. One segment for an uninterrupted job; three for one interrupted twice. `actual_duration_minutes` is their sum, and the segments are the record it is computed from.
fields.label: Time Segments

name: Farm Task Assignment
